quotes.quote: We present Parametric CAD Bench v3, a 100-task benchmark comprising 30 text-to-CAD creation tasks, 30 text-to-CAD create-and-edit tasks, and 40 tasks that reconstruct mechanical parts from engineering drawings.
Producing an executable CAD script is not sufficient to establish that an agent has satisfied an engineering design request.
Mei Chen Yu Xia Haipeng Mao gNucleus AI, Inc. gNucleus AI, Inc. gNucleus AI, Inc.
Our central question is whether general-purpose AI agents can produce geometrically correct, specification-consistent, parametric CAD artifacts across three workflows.
In create-and-edit, the agent first constructs the base from text and then produces the edited model; both artifacts are graded.
Image-to-CAD tasks provide engineering drawings rather than the held-back dimensional specification.
Table 1 describes the released task composition.
The held-back grader specification also states how each parameter is checked.
Only 8 of the plate's 86 parameters and 7 of the connector's 44 are bound to witnesses on the final geometry; the task's param_check.py measures the rest from native sketch and feature geometry.
CAD engineers wrote the parameter-checking logic shipped in each task's tests/grader/param_check.py.
The 100 final reference models contain 687 solid-modeling feature objects in total, with a mean of 6.87, a median of 6, and a range of 1-20 features per task.
The runtime uses FreeCAD 1.1.0, Harbor 0.23.0, and task schema 1.3.
Reference geometry and task-specific grader assets are placed in a separate verifier environment rather than the agent environment.
The verifier computes two independent axes, geometry_similarity and cad_spec_consistency, using the default v2 scorer in gnucleus-freecad-validator 0.6.0
An independently measured OCCT oriented bounding box is a gate, not an additional weighted subscore: maximum relative error across sorted extents of 10% or more sets g = 0.
Candidates with more than 5,000 faces, or face/vertex counts differing from the reference by more than 50% of the larger count, are rejected.
The default scalar relative tolerance is 1%, with case-specific measurement logic and binding tolerances where applicable.
The default v2 failure budget is 10:
For n ≥ 10, each failed or unmeasurable parameter costs 0.1, preventing large specifications from diluting failures.
This continuous reward is not Pass@1.
Final exception outcomes contribute zero.
Thus a zero score on a required axis or deliverable cannot be rescued by another axis.

Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 achieves the highest overall point estimate, 61.03%, followed by mini-swe-agent with the same model at 57.96%, Codex with GPT-6 Astra at 56.87%, and Claude Code with Claude Fable 5.1 at 56.75%.
Point-estimate ordering alone does not demonstrate a statistically decisive ranking.
With Opus 5.5 held constant, Claude Code exceeds mini-swe-agent by 3.08 points.
These comparisons remain conditional on the evaluated configurations and dates, including different Claude Code versions; they are not completely controlled model or agent ablations.
Across the 13 rows, its mean reward ranges from 8.18% to 84.66%, a 76.49-point spread.
However, these scores measure that entire workflow, not visual perception in isolation: CAD construction, tool use, image transport, and failure recovery can all affect the outcome.
Codex with GPT-6 Astra has the lowest ratio among all 13 systems: $317.81 divided by 56.87 points, or $5.59 per point.
This descriptive ratio measures expenditure per achieved score point, not the marginal cost of improving a system by one point.
The benchmark is a curated 100-task FreeCAD evaluation, not a representative sample of all engineering CAD.
Grader rewards are heuristic proxies: geometric similarity and checked parameters do not certify all future edits, design intent, or engineering validity.
Single official attempts do not establish run-to-run robustness.
Known API costs exclude some compute and hosting costs.
The reported runs use Harbor 0.23.0, FreeCAD 1.1.0, and gnucleus-freecad-validator 0.6.0, published on PyPI and tagged v0.6.0 (commit 2a5d67f) in the validator repository.
The benchmark tasks, including their specifications, reference models, and drawings, were authored by gNucleus AI and are released under the Apache License 2.0, as is the validator.

V3 is the latest version and contains 100 complex FreeCAD tasks: 30 creation tasks from text, 30 create-and-edit tasks from text, and 40 creation tasks from engineering drawings.
Scores are on a 0-100 scale. Overall is the mean reward across all 100 tasks; failures count as zero.
Scoring is deterministic - same output, same score.
Two Claude Opus 5.5 results join the V3 leaderboard.
Claude Code reaches 61.03% and mini-swe-agent with the multimodal bridge reaches 57.96%, with both systems setting new image-to-CAD highs.
A benchmark for AI agents that design parametric 3D mechanical parts.
The agent must then produce a script that, when executed by FreeCAD, creates a saved CAD document for that part.
FreeCAD is open source, fully scriptable from Python, and has a stable native format (.FCStd) that preserves the full feature history.
Plenty of models can produce a 3D solid that matches a reference volume.
The bench measures that loop end-to-end rather than just the first model output.
This is the editability gate, expressed as arithmetic.
The agent receives only the natural-language part description and the parameter table - never the reference CAD file.
The three suites are complementary, not competing.

means the reference geometry, validator, and scorer are sealed into each task image at root-only paths the agent can't read, so the evaluation is fully reproducible from the image alone.
Early results show GPT-5.5 via Codex leading at 0.832, with a visible harness effect: swapping the driver while keeping the model fixed shifts scores by roughly 10% in either direction.

The new release keeps the 100-task parametric CAD format while updating the modeling runtime, correcting the evaluation harness, and starting a fresh leaderboard with the latest generation of frontier models and agents.
FreeCAD moved from 0.21.2 to 1.1.0.
In v1, the grader package, structured specification, and reference geometry lived in the same task image behind filesystem permissions.
The validator is updated from 0.1.0 to 0.4.0.
That makes a v2 score a measurement on a new benchmark version, not a continuation of the v1 series.
Score is mean continuous task reward.
A perfect result earns 1.0, partial results receive partial credit, and failed or unscored trials count as zero.
Claude Fable 5.1 leads with 84.81%, only 0.02 points ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 84.78%.
That difference is well within their overlapping 95% confidence intervals, so we treat the two results as statistically equivalent on this 100-task sample.
V2 contained 100 text-to-CAD creation tasks.
V3 uses a new 30/30/40 cohort spanning creation, create-and-edit, and image-to-CAD.

The image tasks provide an engineering drawing rather than a natural-language feature specification, while create-and-edit tests whether an agent can understand and modify an existing parametric model.

The runtime remains pinned to FreeCAD 1.1.0, while the updated scorer uses an oriented-bounding-box size gate, stricter per-component comparisons, revised geometry weights, and stronger spatial alignment scoring.
V3 uses Harbor 0.23.0 and task schema 1.3 against one immutable dataset digest.
Each official row is a fresh 100-task cohort with one attempt per task and four-way concurrency.
Only narrowly defined infrastructure failures may be replaced, with the original attempt retained; model, tool, timeout, verifier, and output failures otherwise remain zero.

quotes.quote: A v3 score is therefore a fresh benchmark measurement, not a continuation of the v2 series.
Overall score is the mean continuous reward across all 100 tasks.
A perfect result earns 1.0, partial results receive partial credit, and failed or unscored trials count as zero.
The 95% confidence interval is calculated over the 100 per-task rewards.
GPT-6 Astra leads the public v3 leaderboard at 56.87%, only 0.12 percentage points ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 at 56.75%.

Their 95% confidence intervals overlap substantially, as does Claude Opus 5's third-place interval, so the point-estimate ordering among the top three should not be read as a statistically decisive separation on this 100-task cohort.
Gemini 3.8 Flash paired with mini-swe-agent (with multimodal bridge) reaches 36.19% overall and 31.10% on image-to-CAD, compared with 27.56% overall and 17.45% on image-to-CAD for Antigravity.

This is not a perfectly controlled agent ablation-the prompts, tool protocols, and serving paths differ-but it shows that the way an agent exposes images can materially change the measured capability of the same named model.
A custom observation template bypasses mini-swe-agent's normal 10,000-character shell-output truncation whenever the multimodal marker is present, preserving the complete data URL.
In all 40 image-to-CAD trajectories for each public mini-swe-agent run, the original drawing appears as the first tool result.
mini-swe-agent's mean advantage is 13.65 percentage points on this cohort (paired 95% CI: 5.55 to 21.75), but it uses more tokens, time, and money.
The bridge enables direct visual reasoning without giving mini-swe-agent a native image-view tool; it does not make the interaction as efficient or robust as a first-class visual interface.
If the model names a nonexistent derived crop, the shell error can land between the markers and be forwarded as though it were encoded image bytes.
That happened in six Gemini image-to-CAD trials.
They were agent/adapter failures, not transient infrastructure failures, so all six remain zero and were not selectively retried.
This diagnosis documents a limitation of the evaluated interface; it must not become a source of benchmark-specific prompt tuning.
Six of the 100 tasks receive zero reward from every evaluated row, and all six are create-and-edit tasks.
Across all 11 rows, image-to-CAD averages 32.28%, versus 42.54% for creation and 30.74% for create-and-edit, but image-to-CAD also has the largest variation between systems.
GPT-6 Astra is both the highest-scoring row and the most cost-efficient row in this matrix: it costs $317.81 for the full cohort, or $5.59 per percentage point of leaderboard score.
Model tier or per-token price is a poor proxy for the cost of completing an agentic workload.
Astra reports the fewest tokens in the matrix despite leading the benchmark.

The primary metric is mean continuous task reward, combining geometry similarity and specification consistency.
Scores therefore reflect graded performance across tasks rather than a binary task-success rate.

The validator reports geometry_similarity (solid count, volume, surface area, bounding box, surface-type distribution), cad_spec_consistency (named driven dimensions matching the part spec within tolerance), and a harmonic-mean composite of the two.
Each row in this dataset describes one parametric CAD part.
